id_and_class.summary: Alyssa Ney holds that the world is fundamentally the way physics says it is, and that consciousness is real but not fundamental, arising from or realized by the physical. Physicalism in her sense is a claim about what is fundamental, not about what exists, so it does not require eliminating consciousness any more than it requires eliminating spaghetti.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Real but Not Fundamental

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a non-fundamental part of the physical world, arising from or realized by what fundamental physics describes.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind arises from or is realized by the physical. Ney does not require that consciousness be reduced to something easily definable in current physics.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence (consciousness is realized by the physical and is not fundamental)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Ney counts intentionality, like consciousness and free will, as real but not fundamental.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Whatever fundamental physics posits, plus non-fundamental phenomena (consciousness, intentionality, free will, everyday objects) that exist without appearing in physics.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Ney expects the methods of physics to eventually supply the tools to understand consciousness, while rejecting scientism, which she defines with Susan Haack as uncritical deference to science and blindness to its fallibility.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal consciousness, intentionality, and free will as non-fundamental phenomena.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Physicalism stated as a thesis about how the world is fundamentally, which leaves room for real phenomena that physics does not mention.
core_claims_and_evidence: The world is fundamentally the way physics says it is.
Physics does not mention spaghetti, yet spaghetti exists, because it does not exist fundamentally; the same holds for consciousness.
Physicalists who reject whatever physics does not mention go beyond what physicalism requires.
Dualists and panpsychists give up too early on the scientific project, since there is no good reason to think physics will never explain consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: metaphysics of fundamentality informed by physics.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Claims that consciousness is realized by the physical can look brute or unintelligible to skeptics. Ney replies that every theory stops somewhere, and that the dispute turns on differing standards for a valid explanation.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Ney offers no specific account of how physical processes realize consciousness; she defends the framework within which such an account should be sought. Anyone who rejects the scientific framework will find no materialist explanation satisfying.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent within a physicalism built around fundamentality, and it separates that physicalism from both reductive and eliminativist versions.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since consciousness here is realized by the physical, it does not continue once its physical basis is gone.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Ney's Physicalism, Not Scientism (Landscape of Consciousness entry), Alyssa Ney
